meta.usefulness_scale: 1 = rarely needed, mostly color -> 5 = essential, daily use
meta.note: First batch of 50 entries: basic etiquette -> general/teen slang -> thrift-market vocab -> skate. See /sources for citations.

sources.timeout-bkk-2026: Time Out Bangkok, 'Gen Z Thai slang: 8 words you'll hear in Bangkok right now', Tita Honghirunkham, Jul 21 2026 - https://www.timeout.com/bangkok/things-to-do/gen-z-thai-slang
sources.smartlocal-2024: TheSmartLocal Thailand, 'Guide to Thai Slang', updated 11 Mar 2024 - https://thesmartlocal.co.th/thai-slang-guide/
sources.thaipod101: ThaiPod101.com, 'Must-Know Thai Slang Words and Phrases' lesson series - https://www.thaipod101.com
sources.psu-orientation: Prince of Songkla University orientation materials, 'Thai Etiquette in Communication' - https://gao.psu.ac.th/images/orientation/2025/lessons/05_Thai_Language.pdf
sources.learnthaiwithmod: Learn Thai With Mod, 'Giving a Compliment and More Slangs' - https://learnthaiwithmod.com/2012/11/learn-thai-giving-a-compliment-and-more-slangs/
sources.bargain-guides: Cross-checked across ThaiPod101 'Survival Phrases: Lower the Price Please', thelongestwayhome.com bargaining guide, and related Thai market-phrase guides
sources.secondhand-source: Pre-Loved Podcast, episode on secondhand shopping in Thailand (Cavina interview) - https://prelovedpod.libsyn.com/
sources.general-vocab: Standard/basic Thai vocabulary, not tied to a single article

entries.actual_meaning: hello / general greeting, any time of day
entries.example_th: สวัสดีครับ ผมชื่อมัคส์
entries.usage_note: always paired with khrap (male) or kha (female)

entries.actual_meaning: polite sentence-ending particle, male speakers
entries.example_th: ขอบคุณครับ
entries.usage_note: softens and adds respect to any sentence

entries.actual_meaning: polite sentence-ending particle, female speakers
entries.example_th: ขอบคุณค่ะ
entries.usage_note: falling tone for statements, rising tone (คะ) for questions

entries.actual_meaning: thank you
entries.example_th: ขอบคุณมากครับ
entries.usage_note: add 'mak' for emphasis

entries.actual_meaning: no worries / it's okay / you're welcome
entries.example_th: ไม่เป็นไรครับ
entries.usage_note: also the go-to phrase when a haggle doesn't land

entries.actual_meaning: sorry / excuse me
entries.example_th: ขอโทษครับ ขอทางหน่อย
entries.example_romanized: kho thot khrap, kho thang noi

entries.actual_meaning: how are you? / are you well?
entries.example_th: สบายดีไหมครับ
entries.usage_note: reply with 'sabai dee' plus khrap/kha

entries.actual_meaning: the palms-together, slight-bow greeting gesture
entries.example_th: เขาไหว้ผู้ใหญ่ทุกครั้ง
entries.example_romanized: khao wai phu yai thuk khrang
entries.usage_note: hand height signals the level of respect shown

entries.actual_meaning: good luck
entries.example_th: โชคดีนะ

entries.actual_meaning: gorgeous, fabulous, top-tier — an enthusiastic stamp of approval
entries.example_th: ชุดนี้เริ่ดมาก
entries.usage_note: say it flat for matter-of-fact, or drawn out ('reerrdd') for drama

entries.speak_text: สองเท่าสิบ
entries.actual_meaning: a deliberately low score for something secretly too good to share — gatekeeping as criticism
entries.example_th: ร้านนี้ 2/10 ห้ามไปนะ
entries.example_romanized: rahn ni song tem sip, ham pai na
entries.example_en: This place is a 2/10 — don't go (it's actually amazing).
entries.usage_note: deep internet vernacular, credited to Gen Alpha

entries.actual_meaning: underwhelming, disappointing — a verbal shrug
entries.example_th: งานเลี้ยงเมื่อคืนอ่อมไปหน่อย
entries.example_romanized: ngan liang meua khuen aum pai noi
entries.example_en: Last night's party was kind of a letdown.
entries.usage_note: softer than saying something was outright boring

entries.actual_meaning: went all out, nailed it, delivered beyond expectations
entries.example_th: เขาทำถึงมากงานนี้
entries.example_romanized: khao tam teung mak ngan ni
entries.example_en: They really went all out on this one.
entries.usage_note: rare slang term used with zero irony

entries.actual_meaning: to prank or trick someone, usually without malice — 'got played'
entries.example_th: โดนแกงอีกแล้ว
entries.usage_note: usually playful; can turn awkward if the target isn't laughing

entries.actual_meaning: lol / laughing out loud in text
entries.example_th: 5555 ตลกมาก
entries.usage_note: more 5s = harder laughter

entries.actual_meaning: euphoric, blissful, deeply satisfying
entries.example_th: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวร้านนี้ฟินมาก
entries.example_en: The noodles here really hit the spot.
entries.usage_note: often paired with 'mak' (very)

entries.actual_meaning: said to manifest good wishes after a compliment or kind words
entries.example_th: สาธุ ขอให้เป็นจริง
entries.example_en: Amen, I hope that comes true.
entries.usage_note: often paired with a wai

entries.actual_meaning: delicious/spicy — also used for someone hot or stylish
entries.example_th: ส้มตำแซ่บมาก
entries.example_en: This papaya salad is so good.
entries.usage_note: also spelled zap/zaap; can compliment looks too

entries.actual_meaning: just for fun, not serious, casual
entries.example_th: เล่นขำๆ อย่าซีเรียส
entries.example_en: Just playing around, don't take it seriously.

entries.actual_meaning: annoying, irritating
entries.example_th: อย่าลำไยน่า
entries.usage_note: can be lighthearted between friends

entries.actual_meaning: an affectionate lead-in meaning roughly 'what a cutie'
entries.example_th: ไอ้ต้าวน่ารักอะไรเบอร์นี้
entries.example_romanized: ai tao na-rak arai boe ni
entries.usage_note: Thais tend to drag out the last consonant for effect

entries.actual_meaning: imaginary, made-up — e.g. 'fan tip' = imaginary partner
entries.example_th: รวยทิพย์
entries.usage_note: attach to any noun to mean 'imaginary ___'

entries.actual_meaning: excellent, stunning, the bomb
entries.example_th: หน้าคุณวันนี้สุดปังเลย
entries.example_romanized: na khun wan-ni sud pang loei

entries.literal_meaning: a fishing trap (breaking = fish spilling out)
entries.actual_meaning: cat's out of the bag, a secret gets revealed
entries.example_th: โป๊ะแล้วไง

entries.actual_meaning: a nosy person/snoop, after Marvel's Black Widow (Natasha Romanoff)
entries.example_th: ระวังนะ มีนาตาชาอยู่ในกลุ่ม
entries.example_romanized: rawang na, mee Natasha yoo nai klum
entries.example_en: Careful, there's a snoop in the group chat.
entries.usage_note: meme-based, niche

entries.actual_meaning: money, casual everyday word
entries.example_th: ไม่มีตังค์เลย
entries.example_en: I don't have any money at all.

entries.actual_meaning: to hype someone up, praise excessively
entries.example_th: อย่าอวยกันเกินไป
entries.example_en: Don't hype each other up too much.

entries.actual_meaning: over the top, exaggerated
entries.example_th: เว่อร์ไปแล้ว

entries.actual_meaning: to trick, deceive, or con someone
entries.example_th: เธอถูกเขาต้มแล้ว
entries.usage_note: older, more established synonym of gaeng

entries.actual_meaning: unexpected good luck, a lucky break
entries.example_th: วันนี้ส้มหล่นจริงๆ
entries.example_romanized: wan ni som lon jing jing
entries.example_en: Today was such a lucky break.

entries.actual_meaning: to rush through work sloppily just to finish it
entries.example_th: อย่าเผางานสิ

entries.actual_meaning: to throw a tantrum
entries.example_th: อย่าวีนแตกสิ

entries.literal_meaning: playful slur of 'chai mai' (isn't that right?)
entries.actual_meaning: right? / isn't that so? — said playfully
entries.example_th: เธอชอบเพลงนี้ชิมิ
entries.example_romanized: ther chorb pleng ni chi mi
entries.usage_note: cutesy, playful tone

entries.actual_meaning: informal sentence-ending particle that softens a statement or question
entries.example_th: จะไปไหนอ่ะ
entries.usage_note: stretch it out ('aaaa') for extra whine/drama

entries.actual_meaning: casual yes/no question particle, same job as 'mai'
entries.example_th: ไปกันป่ะ

entries.actual_meaning: cool, stylish
entries.example_th: รองเท้าคู่นี้เท่มาก
entries.usage_note: written without the silent ห์ — a common spelling mix-up

entries.actual_meaning: to brag/boast (Central Thai); in the Southern dialect it instead means 'to lie'
entries.example_th: อย่าโม้น่า
entries.example_en: Stop bragging (or, in the South: stop lying).
entries.usage_note: genuine regional-meaning flip worth knowing in the South

entries.actual_meaning: a braggart, someone who exaggerates or lies a lot
entries.example_th: เขาเป็นคนขี้โม้

entries.actual_meaning: more than a friend but not officially a partner — a 'situationship'
entries.example_th: เขามีกิ๊กหลายคน
entries.example_en: He's got a few situationships going.

entries.actual_meaning: netizens, people who post/argue online
entries.example_th: ชาวเน็ตดราม่ากันใหญ่
entries.example_en: The internet is in an uproar over this.

entries.actual_meaning: slang for 'the internet' / mobile data
entries.example_th: เน็ตหมดแล้ว

entries.actual_meaning: how much? (asking a price)
entries.example_th: อันนี้เท่าไหร่ครับ
entries.usage_note: the opening line of every haggle

entries.actual_meaning: that's too expensive
entries.example_th: แพงไปหน่อยนะ
entries.usage_note: your first counter after hearing the price

entries.actual_meaning: can you give a discount?
entries.example_th: ลดได้ไหมครับ
entries.usage_note: say it with a smile, not an attitude

entries.actual_meaning: no thanks / I don't want it — the classic walk-away line
entries.example_th: ไม่เอาแล้วครับ ขอบคุณ
entries.example_romanized: mai ao laeo khrap, khob khun
entries.usage_note: walking away calmly after this often gets a better offer

entries.thai_script: ลองใส่ได้ไหม
entries.actual_meaning: can I try it on?
entries.example_th: ลองใส่ได้ไหมคะ

entries.actual_meaning: secondhand — the standard Thai term (not 'thrift')
entries.example_th: เสื้อผ้ามือสอง
entries.usage_note: Thais rarely say 'thrifting' — mue song is the everyday word

entries.actual_meaning: a flea market / pop-up weekend market
entries.example_th: ไปตลาดนัดกันไหม
entries.example_en: Want to go to the market?

entries.actual_meaning: to fall — the word you'll hear (and say) constantly while learning to skate
entries.example_th: ล้มอีกแล้ว

entries.actual_meaning: a move, trick, or stance — the generic word for 'a trick'
entries.example_th: ท่านี้ยากมาก
entries.usage_note: actual trick names (ollie, kickflip) are almost always just used in English
